blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: High-quality articulated assets are essential for embodied perception, simulation, and manipulation, yet constructing them at scale remains difficult. Manual annotation and procedural modeling require substantial human effort. Recent agentic systems automate asset construction through program synthesis, but repeat costly reasoning and refinement for every new asset. Our key observation is that assets within a category can share construction logic despite variations in structure and appearance. Agentic synthesis and procedural generation are therefore complementary: agents can construct reusable programs, while procedural execution reuses the resulting logic across many samples. We therefore present RFW-A, which combines the two in a new articulated-asset generation paradigm. Starting from existing articulated programs, RFW-A organizes reusable components and their dependencies into category-level generators. Agents test and refine these generators across sampled configurations and motion states. Once constructed and validated, the generators produce diverse assets through procedural execution with no further model calls or token charges. The estimated API cost of generator authoring averages $10.62, amortizing to $0.05 per asset over 200 assets, versus $1.24 for the sampled per-asset agentic synthesis baseline. Using RFW-A, we built RFW-A-400K, containing over 400K sim-ready articulated assets across more than 500 categories. Experiments show high structural and kinematic validity and stable execution across physics simulators. Beyond asset validity, training with RFW-A-400K improves part-level articulation estimation on seen and unseen categories, while policies trained in simulation with retrieved and program-edited assets transfer zero-shot to real articulated objects.

blocks.en:
Articulated objects are ubiquitous in everyday environments, ranging from
cabinets and appliances to tools and mechanisms, as illustrated in
Figure 1 . Their functionality depends not only on shape, but also on
how their parts are connected and move. High-quality articulated assets are
therefore essential for learning part semantics, kinematics, and interaction
affordances, as well as for training and evaluating manipulation policies in
simulation [ 86 , 57 , 51 , 58 , 82 , 91 , 95 ] . Compared with static 3D
models [ 2 , 16 , 17 ] , these assets
require additional specifications of part hierarchies, joint parameters,
motion ranges, and physical properties. Producing and checking these
annotations requires substantial human effort [ 86 , 51 , 89 ] ; even with purpose-built interfaces, annotation can take
around ten minutes per asset [ 51 ] .

blocks.en:
Procedural generation reduces per-asset effort by encoding construction rules
in a reusable program that can produce many object variants [ 45 ] . Such generators can efficiently scale asset
sampling within an object category, but their construction rules are still
manually authored and are difficult to transfer across categories. Agentic
program synthesis addresses the authoring problem by using language models to
generate, execute, and refine articulated object programs [ 68 , 20 , 97 ] . However, existing systems typically
synthesize assets one at a time, requiring a new round of reasoning and
correction for every output. Thus, procedural generation scales sampling but
not generator authoring, whereas agentic synthesis automates authoring but
repeats the process at the asset level.

blocks.en:
To answer this question, we present RoboFlywheel-Articulation ( RFW-A ), an
agentic procedural generation framework that shifts agentic synthesis from
individual assets to reusable category-level generators
(Figure 3 ). To support variation, each generator
specifies both what can change and which structural relationships must remain
valid. RFW-A organizes these choices and dependencies into a category
blueprint built from reusable components in existing articulated programs.
Agents translate the blueprint into executable code, and iteratively test and
refine it across sampled configurations and motion states. Once constructed
and validated, the generator produces additional assets through procedural
execution with no further model calls or token charges. As summarized in Figure 3 , this
amortizes agentic construction cost across many assets and enables broad and
dense scaling across object categories: in our cost comparison, amortizing
the mean generator-authoring API cost over 200 assets yields $0.05 per asset,
versus $1.24 for the sampled per-asset agentic synthesis baseline
(Figure 6 ).

blocks.en:
Using RFW-A , we build RFW-A -400K, containing 402,410 articulated assets
across more than 500 object categories, approximately 37 times the size of
Articraft, the largest existing articulated-object dataset. Each asset
includes part structure, kinematics, estimated physical properties, and the
parameters needed to reproduce its construction.
Our evaluation shows a 100% asset-level kinematic pass rate over the full
release. On a 200-asset evaluation subset, 99.5% of assets pass a 1-second
passive rollout with the root fixed in all four simulators: Genesis,
PyBullet, MuJoCo, and Isaac Sim.
Downstream experiments further show that training with RFW-A -400K improves
part-level articulation estimation on seen and unseen categories compared
with PartNet-Mobility alone and Articraft augmentation.
We further evaluate its utility for robot learning: across five manipulation
tasks, policies trained from simulated demonstrations using retrieved and
program-edited assets transfer zero-shot to real articulated objects.

blocks.en:
In summary, our contributions are: • We introduce RFW-A , an agentic procedural generation framework
that constructs and validates reusable category-level generators,
enabling asset sampling without per-asset model inference. • Using RFW-A , we release RFW-A -400K, comprising 402,410 articulated
assets across more than 500 object categories. Each asset includes explicit
part structure, kinematics, estimated physical properties, and reproducible
generation parameters. • We evaluate asset quality and cross-simulator compatibility, demonstrate improved part-level articulation estimation on seen and unseen categories, and show zero-shot sim-to-real manipulation using policies trained with retrieved and program-edited RFW-A -400K assets.

blocks.en: 2.1 Articulated Object Datasets
blocks.zh: 2.1 直译对象数据集

blocks.en:
Large-scale 3D repositories provide broad geometric diversity, but most assets
are static and lack reliable part and articulation annotations [ 2 , 16 , 17 ] . Datasets for
articulated objects address this gap by adding part hierarchies, joint
parameters, motion ranges, and actionable part labels to curated CAD models or
real scans [ 75 , 86 , 51 , 22 ] . More
recent releases expand category and structural coverage, and some also include
material or physical-property annotations [ 89 , 28 , 1 ] . Complementing
these annotated collections, RFW-A -400K provides both assets and their
executable construction programs. These programs support resampling and
editing within each defined object family.

blocks.zh: 2.2 设计对象的重建和生成

blocks.en:
Articulated reconstruction methods recover instance geometry and kinematics
from interaction, single- or multi-state images, RGB-D observations, or videos [ 29 , 48 , 79 , 94 ] . Recent methods
use 3D Gaussian Splatting to improve reconstructed geometry and appearance [ 54 , 80 , 81 , 53 , 15 , 67 , 27 , 19 ] .
These approaches can produce detailed digital twins, but they reconstruct a
particular observed object and must infer occluded geometry and ambiguous motion
from the available observations.

blocks.zh: 2.3 程序、程序和代理生成

blocks.en:
Programmatic representations encode 3D construction as CSG trees, assembly
programs, or CAD command sequences. Their explicit operations and parameters
support structured generation and editing [ 66 , 31 , 32 , 83 , 35 , 3 , 40 ] . Procedural generation reuses such programs
across sampled configurations.
Arti-PG synthesizes articulated objects by manipulating structure programs
and propagating annotations [ 70 ] , while Infinigen-Articulated
and Infinite Mobility provide manually designed category-level
generators [ 34 , 45 ] .

LLMs and agents have also been used for code generation and structured 3D or
motion synthesis through programmatic interfaces, tool use, and intermediate
representations [ 69 , 26 , 56 , 5 , 8 , 96 ] . For static shapes, ShapeLib uses LLMs to construct reusable
procedural abstractions and refine a shape-sampling
program [ 33 ] . Recent systems specialize agentic synthesis to
articulated assets by jointly constructing geometry and kinematics as
executable programs [ 20 , 68 , 97 ] . These systems broaden the range of
objects that can be synthesized, but still run generation and refinement for
each asset. RFW-A instead uses agents to construct category-level generators
from existing articulated programs and refine them using configuration and
motion tests. The resulting generators produce new assets through procedural
execution without additional model inference.

blocks.en: 4.2 Material Grounding and Directed Editing
blocks.zh: 4.2 材料定位和定向编辑

blocks.en:
The procedural representation specifies how an asset is built and moves;
material grounding extends it to the appearance and physical properties of
its surfaces. To apply this grounding across the release, each validated
generator records a material-class identifier for each visual surface and
connects it to a shared library built once offline. The library supplies
concrete instances that can be reused across generators and sampled across
assets. After geometry and articulation validation, a single offline pass
assigns each visual surface a class from the controlled taxonomy; performing
this pass after repair ensures that added, removed, or renamed surfaces receive
the correct identifiers.

blocks.en: 7 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 7 结论

blocks.en: We present RFW-A, an agentic procedural generation framework that constructs reusable category-level generators, enabling efficient asset sampling and editing without per-asset model inference. Using RFW-A, we build RFW-A-400K, comprising over 400K articulated assets across 500+ categories with explicit kinematics, fine-grained materials, and estimated physical properties. Our experiments demonstrate substantially reduced generation costs, high structural and kinematic validity, and reliable execution across four simulators. Beyond asset quality, RFW-A-400K improves articulation estimation on seen and unseen categories and enables zero-shot sim-to-real robotic manipulation through retrieved and procedurally edited assets. These results establish RFW-A as a scalable and controllable approach to articulated asset generation for embodied learning.
blocks.zh: 我们提出了RFW-A,这是一个代理程序生成框架,用于建造可重复使用的类别级发电机,从而能够在不进行每个资产模型推论的情况下进行有效的资产取样和编辑。 利用RFW-A,我们建造了RFW-A-400K,由500多类400多件明确资产组成,有明显的动能、精细材料和估计的物理特性。 我们的实验表明,在四个模拟器中,发电成本大幅降低,结构和运动有效性高,而且执行可靠。 除了资产质量之外,RFW-A-400K改进了对所见所未见类别的表述估计,并通过检索和经过程序编辑的资产实现零镜头模拟到实际机器人操作。 这些成果将RFW-A确立为一种可伸缩和可控制的方法,用于为体现的学习创造资产。

blocks.en:
RFW-A allows assets to be resampled and edited without a new agent call,
but diversity remains limited by the source components and category
blueprints. Expanding mechanism and object-family coverage requires extending
these sources or blueprints. The cost benefit depends on construction and repair costs and the
number of valid outputs; broader multi-category studies are needed to
quantify savings and component contributions.
